missions.title: SLIM (JAXA), January 2024
missions.reported: Landed 2024-01-19 15:20 UTC with the solar cells facing west and the Sun in the east. Powered down at 17:57 UTC. JAXA expected power to return as the Sun moved west. Operations resumed on January 28.
missions.computed: Sun at azimuth 82° (east), elevation 37° at landing, so a west-facing array gets nothing. Light first reaches it on 2024-01-23 22:20 UTC, it passes half output on 2024-01-26 09:33 UTC, and it is at 83% on January 28 12:00 UTC.
missions.verdict: The power window opens in the days before operations resumed. The real attitude of the lander was more complex than a vertical west-facing plate, so this checks the geometry, not the exact date.

missions.title: Blue Ghost Mission 1 (Firefly, NASA CLPS), March 2025
missions.reported: Landed 2025-03-02 08:34 UTC. Firefly reports 346 hours of daylight operations, ending about 5 hours into the lunar night.
missions.computed: Sun's center reaches the horizon 347.7 h after landing, and the last 5% of the disk is gone at 348.8 h.
missions.verdict: Within 2 to 3 hours of the reported daylight, on a smooth sphere without local terrain.

missions.title: Chang'e 4 (CNSA), lunar far side
missions.reported: The far side never faces Earth, so the mission communicates through the Queqiao relay satellite.
missions.computed: Over four years the Earth's center never gets higher than -37.1° at the landing site.
missions.verdict: No direct-to-Earth window at any date, as expected.
